_: The changelog up to round 9, frozen (2026-10-05): never edit this file. New changes each add their own fragment beside it (config/changelog/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.json); see src/changelog.ts and CLAUDE.md.

items: Every area now starts with two adults (and a baby) instead of one: the first sieges hit harder, and survival grows more steadily with how well you build your army
Sleeping legends dream: a thought bubble over each shows the sigil of the creature it wants, drawn as that creature's level (a baby's, young's or adult's sigil)
Bring it: put that creature's sigil down anywhere in the legend's area before its wave comes, and the legend wakes happy (its buff on), the area turns friendly, and the creature you brought joins it
When a friendly area's wave comes, its creatures and its legend guard it for you; an area whose legend's wish wasn't granted wakes angry, and its creatures go for your nearest animals or soundsystem
Try it: add ?quest=1 to the link to start beside a legend with what it wants on your stack (press E there)
Your animals leave alone the creature you're inviting while you chat with it (their shots and blasts pass it by); once the chat stops it's fair game again

Fights happen at the camera's scale: creatures in a fight move about as fast as you (12 to 20 m/s), lunge 12 to 16 m in a dash-strike (a line on the ground shows where), and their packs spread out over about 50 m
Land in a wild area and its creatures are onto you within a few seconds, from all sides
Your animals chase attackers up to about 40 m before coming back; shots fly much faster and further; knockback throws creatures well clear; the boar lowers its head (its lane shown) before it charges

Fight scale and speed can be changed live: in the debug panel (~), or [ ] and ; ' (remembered; ?fightScale= and ?fightSpeed= in the link); try the patterns with ?arena=surround, charge, volley, swarm, lob, beam, ambush, burrow, leap, legend, siege...

The ley line now points to your next objective: one softly glowing line from the last runestone you reached to the next, along the valleys, fading from the first area's colour to the next one's. It stays on the ground even from the treetops (glowing through the leaves), and when you reach the next stone the old line drains into it and a new one draws out to the stone after
The hole in the canopy round you on the ground has no hard edge any more: the trees thin out gradually and raggedly, each at its own distance, and rising or landing no longer shows a circle round you
Smooth-barked trees (beech, rowan, hazel) look like trees again: no more grey columns on brown stumps; their trunks are shaded round and marked with the eyes of fallen branches
On the ground, only nearby rune stones keep their wave number at the top of the screen, so far ones no longer pile up there; over the treetops none is held there
The glowing wave numbers no longer float in the sky past the curve of the world: they fade out as their stone goes over the horizon

Home is dressed with its own set: lantern posts, path lights, flower pots, mushroom rings and stepping stones round the dancefloor's clearing, a fairy-lit branch arch over each path, and a speaker stack, crates and a signpost by the treehouse

Wild areas grow: every area starts with one baby and one adult, and each wave every area the party hasn't reached gains another creature, a baby, young or adult. So the longer an area stays wild, the bigger the army that marches when its wave comes, and old wild areas get dangerous to cross on foot. Newcomers turn up out of sight, never popping in
Debug overlay (~): a power meter, your party's fighting strength (on your leash and parked) against each siege's and all the marchers together
A playtest log: every 10 s of play it notes your party, the waves and the sieges on this browser; press L (or open the game with ?playtest=download) to save it as a file to send
Wild creatures go for you as soon as you land in their area (not just when you're close); they still give up when you rise, or once you've left their area and are well away
The creature you're chatting to won't attack you while you talk (its friends still will)
Creatures enraged by a wave (attacking a soundsystem) have angry red eyes and can't be invited
Beaten creatures no longer vanish: they run off, out of the forest, and are gone for good (yours too: a beaten party animal runs away off its leash)
Creatures notice you from further away: they turn to look at you, curious babies come up to you and shy ones keep their distance; fights pick up from further off too

Creatures fight in their own ways: wolves spread out to surround you, hares dart in and back out, boars charge in a straight line (sidestep!), bats swarm without piling up, ravens line up and shoot on the beat, spiders lie still until you come close
New attacks: owls lob shots that land where you were standing (a ring shows where; move out of it), salamanders and spiders burn you with beams
A test arena for creature fights: add ?arena=wolf*4,raven*3 to the link (your side first, @2 for adults); J starts it again

Creatures have traits you can see, as marks by their health bars: fliers (blue) take half from melee, armoured ones (grey square) take a third from shots, lobs and beams but get knocked over and stunned by knockback, swarms (violet) take double from area attacks, heavy ones (brown square) won't be knocked back
A hit that's strong against its target bursts gold with "!!"; one it resists goes "tink"
Moles burrow: a mound of earth races over the ground at you (nothing can hit it) and the mole bursts up under you
Toads leap at you in an arc and slam down: a ring shows where they'll land
Bats screech all round themselves (a ring shows its reach), spiders spit webs (an adult's slows you), beetles plod in slowly but are hard to stop

Wild legends fight with big, slow, telegraphed moves in a pattern: a ground slam (a ring shows its reach), a nova of shots all round (spokes show it coming), and a charge (it backs off, then thunders down a lane you can see)
At half health a wild legend roars (a red burst, the screen shakes) into its second phase: faster, with a beam it spins all the way round (a circle shows its reach), and a red aura

Ley lines: a glowing chain runs through the runestones in the order the waves will wake them, from the last wave's stone on through the next few, each link fainter than the one before. They wander along the valleys between the stones, a shimmer flows along them toward the later stone, and over the treetops they rise above the canopy so you can steer by them (?ley=0 hides them)
Boosting over the hills is smooth again: no more hitches as new ground streams in ahead of you
Wide undergrowth and thickets no longer float at their downhill end on steep slopes

The music takes its mood from Ed's two favourite references: dreamy, ethereal choirs and sung notes over the forest, then harder, darker waves with distorted industrial drums, metal clanks, a gritty bass and string stabs, then breakbeats; the bubblegum and chiptune waves have made way (a flash of chiptune still sparkles in the frenzy)

The music sounds bigger and clearer: crisp 808-style hats, a punchier kick with a click, wide detuned supersaw leads, breathing pads, a darker, deeper reverb, and everything rebalanced so the drums, bass, chords and melodies each have their own space
A big glowing number over every rune stone: the wave that will wake it (dimmed once the party's there)
Every area now has its own legend, asleep for centuries: half sunk into the ground and grown over with moss, easy to mistake for a mound. Walking by won't wake it
When the party reaches its area, the legend heaves up out of the ground, angry, and guards its area: it goes for you, your animals and that area's soundsystem, but never leaves its area
Beat a legend and it sinks back to sleep for good. Home's legend is happy and on your side from the start; press O to make the nearest legend happy (a stand-in until quests): its buff turns on
Party animals now evolve only up to adult: legends are the areas' own

A happy legend guards its area for you: it takes on sieges marching through or on its soundsystem with its big moves, heals between fights, and if it's beaten it sinks back to sleep (its buff gone). See it in the arena: ?arena=home,wolf*6@2!
Flagstones round the dancefloor out past its speakers: rings of mossy old stone where there was bare grass
Auto-talk can be turned off: press 1 or T, or click its button on the action bar (remembered); with it off, hold Shift to talk
A volume slider in the corner (remembered); all the way down mutes
Home is decorated: a ring of lanterns, torches, balloons, fairy lights and candles just outside the dancefloor's clearing

Wild creatures notice you once you're within their attack range or 30 m, and give up when you rise to the treetops, or once you've left their area and are out of range and at least 30 m away; then they wander back home
Melee attackers wind up and lunge at where you were: step aside. Ravens keep their distance and shoot from far off
Party animals following you fight whatever attacks you or them; creatures parked at a sigil guard the ground round it
Nothing attacks babies, on either side: a leash of babies is safe in a fight. Babies never get angry when their area wakes: they stay home and you can still invite them
Berries heal: a party animal that eats one is back to full health (a hurt one goes for berries even if it's a legend), and so is a creature you've just invited, with a green sparkle
The old line of controls in the corner is gone: the action bar shows them (H hides it)
Party witches twirl each other, and play broom limbo: two hold a broom as the bar while a third shuffles under it
Party witches chatting show little emoji bubbles, taking turns
Party witches fly in from just off-screen, so you see them arrive
Lanterns, jam jars, fairy lights and mirror balls hang from the trees in party areas
Talk bubbles and markers sit over a creature's head however big it is, and the grass parts round big creatures as widely as they are
Flying fast over the hills is smooth: you and the camera glide over the bumps, rising early for a crest, instead of jerking up and down
No cliffs on the hills: no slope anywhere is steeper than the camera looks down, so the ground never stretches into streaks or wedges, and the trees on it stand properly (try ?seed=165272)
Rising and landing no longer show a hard-edged circle in the canopy round you, and you're drawn as yourself under the see-through leaves, not as a flat silhouette
The music reacts to the fight: knocked out, it sinks to a muffled, far-off breakdown; near a soundsystem under siege a nervous pulse joins in

The music speeds up as the party grows: from 120 bpm in the quiet forest to about 140 by the finale, easing in a few bars after each wave lands, and everything on the beat (the dancefloor, the lasers, dancing creatures and witches, the border's sparkle) speeds up with it, never skipping a beat

Wild creatures fight back: on the ground, the young and older shoot or lunge at you (watch for the red ring tightening at their feet, and the line a shot will fly along), so dash out of the way. Over the treetops you're safe. Babies never attack
You can still invite creatures while they attack you: big, strong groups are hard to win over without getting hit (a hit doesn't set the chat back; losing a hit is the cost)
You can take three hits (pips under your feet show what's left); one comes back every 20 seconds once you're out of the fight

Knocked out: your sigil stack lets go from the bottom up, a second each, and each creature on your leash goes back to the wild, walking off to an area of its own kind (catch it on the way to invite it again). Creatures at sigils on the ground stay yours: park your army before you scout! Careful leashing legends: if you're knocked out, they go back to the wild too. Then you sparkle home to the treehouse

Party animals fight wild creatures of other kinds near their leash point by themselves; creatures of the same kind never fight each other, whichever side they're on. A beaten wild creature runs off and vanishes; a beaten party animal is lost for good

Sieges: when a wave wakes an area, its wild creatures attack the new soundsystem (a health bar shows over it, and its music crunches as it's damaged). If it falls, its party is over and the attackers march on to the next-nearest soundsystem, the dancefloor included. When every soundsystem has fallen, the run is over
Hits flash and knock creatures back; a legend's quake shakes the screen

New controls, MOBA style: the arrow keys fly (WASD no longer does); Q casts the spell, W dashes, E puts down or picks up a sigil, R cycles the stack; 1 2 3 4 are empty slots for later spells and items. An action bar along the bottom shows all eight with their keys and recharge
Dash: W (gamepad A, touch 'dash') bursts a few metres the way you're steering, on the ground only, about once a second. You can still be hit mid-dash: dash out of a shot's path
The game now runs in fixed steps (60 a second) and draws smoothly between them, ready for co-op
Campfires and bonfires no longer jitter as they flicker: only the flames move

Real music: the party's track is now composed live as you play, every sound synthesised. It moves through sections with the waves: the home speakers' boot is the intro, the forest is gentle and mysterious, each wave builds up and drops as it lands, and the run climbs from melodic forest house through dark synth and chiptune to a phonk finale (?music=drop or ?music=wave7 to hear one part)

Tree trunks are back on the ground: they'd gone black on black in the canopy's shadow, and the big crowns' low boughs hid all but their stumps; trunks now stand clear up to their crowns and stay readable in the dark
No more glowing party cubes
Smoother boosting over the treetops: the work of streaming in new forest, hills and ground is spread across frames, and creatures cost far less to move, so frames stay steady at full speed
Home is a party area too: party things round the dancefloor (never on it)

Real clouds over the treetops: a few soft, see-through clouds drifting high over the curve of the world, glowing in the colours of the party beneath them and pulsing on the beat; now and then one flickers with lightning, sometimes with a forked bolt
Big hills: the forest rolls over broad hills and valleys up to 40 m high, never steep enough to hide you behind a bump (?hills=6 gentle, ?hills=0 flat); the blotchy slope shading is gone
Calmer stars: most barely twinkle, each in its own time
String lights no longer show through the curved earth over the treetops
The arrows at the screen's edge always point the right way, even to things past the curve of the world
The rune stone markers stay on screen: once the stone is in view, the marker floats above it with its countdown, so it's easy to find in a busy forest
Grass grows thicker round the feet of trees and rocks, reeds ring the ponds, and the tufts sit in the canopy's dappled shade like the ground under them
Clouds over the party glow in its colours and pulse on the beat (from the start, over home)
Things stand upright on the hills, planted at their lowest foot: creatures and the witch no longer shear with the slope, and shadows lie neatly on it
?bare=1 shows just the ground, hills and bend under a low moon (?bare=2: grey ground with contour lines), to judge the terrain

Legend buffs: a party legend (an adult you've fed until it evolves) gives you its species' own buff while it lives: faster flight, quicker invites, berries found further off, longer between waves and more. Its sigil shows in a row at the top of the screen (hover for what it does), and a line says what you've gained or lost
Party legends lumber: a creature that evolves into a legend slows to a legend's pace, following you too

Wild legends are rare, late threats: only 3 to 5 a map, far out in remote areas. They're bigger, breathe slowly, and have a dark aura that you can see glowing through the treetops. They sleep until the party reaches their area, then lumber about it (no fighting yet). The legend next to home has gone
The ground rolls: gentle hills and hollows that everything stands on, with the dancefloor, the treehouse, ponds and every path kept level (?hills=0 for flat)

Over the treetops the world curves away, so you see the night sky above the forest: stars, the moon, and slow clouds that glow in the party's colours over partying areas (?curve=0 for flat, ?curve=0.004 for more)

No more Talk button: on the ground the witch chats with the nearest creature in range by herself, on the fly as you move, settling into her talk pose when you stop; move away or rise and the chat pauses, and coming back picks it up
A legend gives you one unimpressed look as you pass, not over and over

Wild creatures are easier to find in the dark: they never sink fully into the shadows, catch a faint rim from your light, and their eyes catch the light now and then; the moonlight is a little cooler and more coloured (?find=0 to compare)

The disco ball no longer shoots lasers; instead each of the 12 speakers round the dancefloor has its own laser, sweeping slowly on the beat to crown the floor in moving beams (damaged speakers flicker theirs, destroyed ones go dark)
Campfires belong to the party now: the sleeping forest has none and is darker for it, and when the party reaches an area its campfires light up with a whoosh of sparks
Flying low and fast, the witch leans into a proper four-frame flying cycle that speeds up the faster you go
Treeless places have tall landmarks now and then: snags in the log piles, cairns and standing stones on the moor, pillars at the stone shrines, rock spires in the ravines

The grass is new: each area's own little tufts (grass, ferns, heather, rushes, moss, clover, needles, fallen leaves, pebbles, the odd flower or mushroom), lit by your light, and only the leafy ones sway
In the wind only the leaves move now: trunks, branches and rocks stay still

Party witches: for every soundsystem playing out in the forest, another witch in her own party outfit flies in to the dancefloor, where she dances (in time with the beat), pairs up to dance, hug, high-five, hold hands, conga or toast, laughs, drinks, runs about, lies back to rest or flies a few laps over the floor
Stand still by the dancefloor for a few seconds and the witch joins the party herself, on her own or with a party witch; move and she stops

Party areas are strewn with party things as the party arrives: tables and chairs, candle rings, glowsticks, deck chairs, crate bars, DJ corners, campfire circles and bonfires, balloons bobbing in the breeze (one even caught up in a tree), cups, cans, confetti and more, in random neons; campfires and lanterns light up their corner
Evolving is much quicker: eating a berry is a quick nibble with a sparkle, and babies evolve after just 1 berry, young after 3, adults after 8
Berries grow in patches of a few bushes, clusters of red glints you can spot
Party animals run to a berry at the same pace they follow you, a quick hop rather than a slow amble
Party animals take berries on their way: following you, they nip over to one near their path; set a sigil in the middle of a patch and they'll eat their way round it
Placed sigils are easier to see: the grass is trampled flat round them, and their runes glow a little brighter
Trunks stay visible in short, dense woods like the tangly forest: only their top part fades where the crowns are hidden
Berries: every area has bushes with shiny dark-red berries (8–12 per area), glowing softly at night and glinting red through the treetops
Party animals walk over to a berry near them and eat it; it grows again somewhere else in the forest

Feed a party animal enough berries and it evolves (babies after 5, young after 10, adults after 30): it glows and pulses for a bar, then flashes into its next size with a burst of sparkles, and the dancefloor flashes in its colour. Adults become legends: the only way to get a party legend
A red ring round each party animal shows how close it is to evolving (near the witch, and just after it eats). Debug: B feeds the nearest party animal a berry
At the start the speakers round the dancefloor boot up one by one, giving you about a minute before the countdown to the first wave begins
A spell: Q (gamepad B, touch 'spell') casts a speed boost: much faster for a few seconds, with a trail; the ring in the corner shows it recharging
Cycle: C (gamepad right-stick click, touch 'cycle') sends the bottom sigil of your stack to the top, so you choose which creature goes down next
A few creatures (hares, stoats, martens) are quick on their feet; legends are very slow; you're still much faster than any of them
The witch is lit by the lights around her: she turns red by a red soundsystem, warm by a campfire, and catches a coloured rim on the side facing a light, while staying easy to see in the dark

Forecasting: the next two areas to join the party are certain, and a few more are likely. Their rune stones grow rings of magic symbols, a full ring of 12 on the next one, and their beams grow as the countdown runs
A smaller, dimmer cue at the screen's edge points to the area after next
Music: a beat plays, loud and clear near the dancefloor and other playing soundsystems, quiet and muffled deep in the forest, and crackling when a speaker nearby is damaged (?music=off)
The new treehouse: a tall timber tower in a giant tree, its turret above the treetops; you start at the decks in its studio, and step down out of it when you set off

Scenes to find: a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a picnic gone wild, an allotment, festival remnants, a cemetery, a car park, a scrap yard, ruined churches and temples, castle ruins and more, each one at most once per map
Tractors, hay bales, fences, gates, lampposts, road signs and other countryside and street finds turn up in the forest, each one at most once per map
No more 'land to talk' prompt
The dancefloor's old soundsystem is gone; its ring of speakers carries the music
The next-stone arrow now points the right way
The next-stone cue shows the area's rune, and its ring fills as the countdown to the next wave runs
The party's border twinkles and flickers between the colours of the areas on either side
Flying straight up or down the screen, the witch is seen from behind or coming at you
Railways and paths no longer run across the dancefloor: they stop, frayed, at the edge of its clearing
Tufts of grass, fern, heather, reeds, moss and clover cover the ground round you, each area its own, swaying in the wind and parting as you and the creatures pass (?grass=0 to 2)
The ground has gentle rises and hollows that your light and the campfires pick out (?relief=0 for flat)
Trees and undergrowth sway in gusts that roll across the forest; gentler over the treetops (?wind=0 for still)
Stronger tilt-shift over the treetops
The game opens close in on the witch in her seat on the treehouse, and eases out as she sets off
The dancefloor is a magic disco floor of glass tiles: dark until you step off the terrace, then it switches on and plays shapes and patterns to the beat, changing on the bar
The floor lights up under you, rippling out on each beat and leaving footprints; landing on it sends a big ripple
It grows wilder as the party spreads: more tiles, more colours, faster changes, more motes; a pulse runs out towards each area the party reaches, and areas with the party add their own shapes
Where two areas meet, their ground textures meander and speckle into each other instead of meeting on a blocky edge (?blend=off to compare)

The standing stones round the dancefloor are now twelve stone speakers, twice as far out, thumping on the beat: the ones beyond the floor face in, the near ones face out, so you always see their fronts (K cycles them through damaged and destroyed, for testing)
The dancefloor's clearing is wider, and the treehouse stands outside the speaker ring
The forest is dark again: the witch's light only reaches as far as the gap in the canopy round her, and the moonlight and twilight fill are lower
Tree trunks fade out at the top in pixel steps where the crowns are hidden, instead of ending in a flat cut
Paths, roads, tracks and streams fray out at their ends instead of stopping square
Creatures, soundsystems and the rune stones are never made see-through round the witch; only the scenery is
Each wave now wakes just one area, chosen as soon as the last one woke, bordering the party and spreading in lobes rather than a circle; its rune stone is the one that wakes
A new pixel cue at the screen's edge points to the next stone to wake, with its distance; the music cue is bigger and pixelled
Awake rune stones can show a thin laser straight up, a column of light, or both (?rune=beam|column|both)
M shows a minimap of the party's spread (debug)
Witch walks 10% faster
Leashes arc gently and their dots flow back towards you
Treetop turns are tight when you're slow; the big skid only comes at speed
The rune stones' beam and laser now rise from the top of the stone
Paths keep one look for their whole length, and run on unbroken past clearings
Every ruin, freak tree, relic, set piece and playground or sports ground is one of a kind: you'll find each at most once per map, facing either way
Stone stairs are a rare find by ravines, rocky slopes, cave mouths and stone shrines, not a path fitting
Soundsystems and set pieces stand clear of the paths
Nothing floats any more: trees, rocks, ruins, the treehouse and set pieces all stand on the ground, and big scenery keeps clear of the soundsystems
Fewer ruins, rocks, relics, stairs and bridges: each is a find now, not clutter
The witch's own light is a tighter pool round her that fades out within about 40 m (try ?glow=50,2.5 to tune it)

Garden walls stand in joined runs along the paths, with flower beds in rows beside them; shrine stones stand in circles; hedges, brambles and rock walls run in lines; water, reeds and boulders gather in clumps, with open ground between
The edge of the see-through hole in the treetops round the witch fades smoothly (no dither)

Big rune stones now mark where every soundsystem will come, glowing with their area's creature's sigil. The next wave's stones wake: they pulse to the beat, throw light and motes, brighter as the wave nears, and send a beam above the trees; when the party arrives the stone flares and sinks as its soundsystem appears. The random rune stones are gone
Points where a branch line leaves the railway
Tapping the start screen on a phone starts the game again, wherever you tap

Along the railways: old wagons, a carriage with a tree through it, little platforms, signal gantries and posts, and buffer stops where the track ends; bridges where paths cross streams, level crossings, stairs into rocky hollows, and verge posts along the roads
Relics of the modern world turn up now and then, more by the roads and railways: a car nose-down in the moss, shopping trolleys, cones, broken highway, a phone box, a sofa, a fridge full of fireflies
A few overgrown playgrounds and sports grounds (tennis, football, baseball, basketball) lie in clearings of their own
Each kind of area has its own mix of tree heights and its own ruins, rocks and odd trees
The ground has shape: moonlit mounds, dark hollows and ridges where the area has them, and more pools in the boggy ones
Each forest now has its own kind of UK tree (oak, beech, Scots pine, yew…), in a range of heights, with leafy trunks
Speech bubbles are pixel outlines, and the emoji in them are bigger pixel art

Above the treetops she has momentum: hold a direction to build up to a boost (the camera draws back a little), swoop round in arcs, skid on a sharp turn, and glide when you let go. The ground stays snappy
Paths wind between the areas, their look changing with each area (dirt tracks, flagstones, root paths, boardwalks...), and some peter out
Old roads sweep across the forest, and two to four railway lines curve across it, broken in places with trees growing between the sleepers
Bushes crowd along the edges of paths and tracks
Streams wind through the forest, and join the wet areas
Ruins, rocks and strange trees turn up here and there to discover
You start sitting on the terrace of the witch's treehouse, by the dancefloor; move or rise to take off
Removed the diagonal stripes across the forest (moonbeams are off; ?moonbeams=on brings them back)
When a tree stands in front of the witch, you now see her through a soft round window that fades in gently, not a square
Land first to talk or to put down and pick up sigils, with new poses
Talking to a creature keeps its progress for a while if you break off
Placed sigils show above the canopy from the treetops
Waves every 5 minutes by default; pick how often on this screen
A small arrow points the way to the music
Slower lasers, party motes drifting over whole areas, and party light on the treetops
Woods have groves, thickets, glades and lone trees, and areas blend into each other
G shows metre rulers and a ground grid
The witch's glow lights up a much wider pool of forest round her
Fewer bushes
Trees no longer pop in and out as you fly
The witch is never lost: tall things in front of her fade, and her silhouette shows through
No more speech icons over every creature in range
String lights hang in long garlands from tree to tree
Soundsystems face different ways
Set pieces are bigger, and areas have ragged edges
The witch has rise and descend poses
Sigils show rings, and creatures show when they're ready to talk
